critic_notes.rationale: This is a direct rediscovery of the canonical value-plus-quality combination (BM × profitability, cf. Novy-Marx/QMJ), and swapping raw margin for an industry rank is a cosmetic refinement rather than a new mechanism.

Sales-to-price and margin improvement are each known, but conditioning the sales-yield value signal on a five-year *trend* in operating margin is a genuinely dynamic (not level-based) interaction that is distinct from the standard static value-quality cross, though the 5-year TREND window will cost coverage and reduce turnover-relevant timeliness.

Internally consistent and correctly signed, but it is essentially E/P × (negative accruals) — a mechanical crossing of two of the most heavily published anomalies (earnings yield and Sloan accruals) that has been extensively documented as earnings-quality-screened value.

Beyond being another EV-yield × profitability quality-value rediscovery, the EV denominator can go negative for net-cash firms, which flips the ratio's sign and makes the cheapest-looking names appear expensive (or vice versa) — a construction flaw that will contaminate the extreme sorts.

The INDICATOR gate collapses roughly half the cross-section (all below-industry-profitability firms, cheap and expensive alike) to exactly zero, producing massive ties, a degenerate short leg, and unstable portfolio composition — and the underlying idea is just the same profitability-screened value trade as proposal 1.

Net-cash-to-market is a balance-sheet-composition valuation measure distinct from BM/EY, and gating it on operating profitability gives an economically coherent "cheap operating business that is not burning cash" story with a sign that matches the expression's natural direction.

The two legs multiply to (oibdp−xint)/(ME+dltt+dlc), i.e. a rank-decomposed restatement of the already-evaluated After-Interest Claim Yield (and structurally a twin of Scalable Sales Claim Value), so it is a rediscovery rather than a new mechanism.

It reuses the archived sales-to-claims value leg but swaps in an accrual-free, three-year-smoothed cash-conversion condition, which is a substantive (if incremental) change to the profitability channel and worth one test, though its implicit product is close to a plain cash-flow-to-enterprise-value yield.

This is a window-and-denominator tweak of the archived Cheap Sales Margin Upswing, whose FMB slope and long-short alpha already carried opposite signs — a symptom the proposal does not diagnose, so shortening the trend window is a cosmetic variant rather than a fix.

Both legs are near-monotone inversions of the archived Scalable Sales Claim Value's components, so the signal is largely the mirror image of an existing test and offers essentially no new information beyond a sign flip.

The expression matches the stated hypothesis and the R&D add-back is an economically motivated correction to the profitability leg, but the sales-to-price value leg and R&D intensity are each well-documented anomalies, so the incremental novelty rests entirely on the interaction.

This introduces a genuinely different value channel (payout yield) than the archive's sales/asset-based ones and is internally consistent, though quality-screened dividend yield is close to well-known practitioner strategies and the mass of zero-dividend firms will pile up at the bottom rank and degrade the short leg.

Depreciation-to-price is a genuinely less-explored capital-intensity value proxy and the gate (oibdp − dp = post-depreciation operating income) is internally coherent with the stated hypothesis, though the signal remains structurally close to the archive's asset-cheapness × profitability family and risks loading mostly on capital intensity rather than mispricing.

Dividend yield × profitability is essentially the well-documented "dividend safety / high-yield quality" screen, and mechanically dvc is zero or missing for most firms, so the rank product collapses to a large tied mass and the signal is effectively profitability among payers only.

This reuses the archive's Net-Cash Profitable Value first term verbatim and merely swaps the profitability level for its second difference (a construction already probed via TREND in Reactivating Asset Value), making it a cosmetic variant that also replaces the archive's only positive-alpha component with a noisier estimator.

SG&A-to-price as an organizational-capital value proxy conditioned on rising gross profit per unit of SG&A is a substantively distinct construction from the archive's revenue- and asset-based value gates, and the expression matches the hypothesis with a coherent positive sign, with the main caveat that xsga/price will be materially correlated with sales-to-price.

Asset-to-market × high, stable gross margin is close to the canonical value-plus-gross-profitability combination and recombines two already-tested archive components (Reactivating Asset Value's at/mve gate and Durable Cash-Flow Value's level-plus-stability SUMRANK), while a 3-period VOL of annual margins is too short to measure stability reliably.

This is the short-side mirror of the standard value-meets-quality trade ("expensive junk underperforms") and a near-duplicate of the archive's Glamour Profit Fade with the profitability delta swapped for level-plus-volatility, so it adds little beyond an already-tested and statistically weak construction.

The second leg is literally identical to the archived "Serviceable Leverage Discount" profitability term and the first leg is "Liquid Distribution Capacity" minus dividends, so this is a mechanical recombination of two already-tested legs rather than a new mechanism.

The interaction leg only swaps TREND(3) for DELTA(1) on the same xint/gross-profit burden used in the archived "Interest-Burden Compression Value," a cosmetic re-parameterization that inherits that signal's noisy denominator (gross profit near zero) without diagnosing why it produced a strong slope but zero alpha.

R&D-to-market-cap is a well-documented published anomaly (Chan-Lakonishok-Sougiannis, Lev-Sougiannis) and COALESCE(xrd,0) forces a large fraction of firms to an identical zero rank, creating massive ties and an unstable long leg, while the margin term is copied verbatim from the archived "RnD-Adjusted Revenue Value."

Internally coherent and cleanly specified, but it reuses the exact value leg of the archived "Productive SGA Platform Value" and replaces TREND(gross profit/SG&A) with a highly correlated revenue-minus-SG&A growth spread, so it is likely to reproduce that signal's high-t-stat/zero-alpha profile rather than resolve it.

The funds-flow coverage leg (oancf over dp+xint) is a genuinely different economic screen from the archived post-depreciation ROA version and the sign logic is consistent, though it retains the dp/market value leg that already delivered a robustly negative FF5 alpha, so the proposal should explain why coverage rather than profitability level flips that outcome.

The expression, hypothesis, and negative expected sign are mutually consistent and the liquidity-scaled valuation denominator is a real departure from the failed "Glamour Profit Fade," but it risks being a repackaged expensive-plus-unprofitable (distress/profitability) composite and the che+dlc denominator can be near zero for cash-poor, debt-free firms.

This is a pure operator swap (MIN for MUL) on the identical two legs of the archive's "Short-Debt Coverage Liquidity Value," i.e. exactly the kind of cosmetic variant of an existing signal that adds no new economic content since rank-product and rank-min are highly collinear.

The numerators are unchanged from the archived "Liquid Distribution Capacity" and the only edits are denominator swaps borrowed from two other already-tested signals (+dlc in the value leg, cogs+xsga in the quality leg), making it a recombination of known winning legs rather than a new mechanism; the stated rationale about avoiding zero-payer ties is also inapt since the original already pooled dvc with cash.

Separating near-term net liquidity (che−dlc) from total net cash while moving long-term debt into the valuation denominator is a genuinely different balance-sheet decomposition from the archived net-cash and short-debt-coverage signals, and the sign logic matches the expression, though the profitability leg is a standard workhorse so the incremental information is modest.

Substituting operating cash flow for SG&A in the liquid-resources numerator is an economically meaningful change of theme (self-funding vs. organizational platform) rather than a rescaling, but adding a stock (che) to an annual flow (oancf) is dimensionally crude and the result will likely be dominated by the well-known cash-flow-to-price effect.

The proposal is internally consistent and, unlike the other entries, is explicitly motivated by the diagnosed fmb/alpha divergence in the sales-yield family, but sales-to-price times gross/operating profitability is close to a textbook value-quality composite and the che/at buffer is a light addition to a leg that has already failed three times on alpha.

This is effectively a re-parameterization of the archived "Cash-Runway Glamour Burn" (same negated after-interest profitability leg, same cash-versus-short-debt-versus-market-value cheapness leg, just rearranged) and it also largely mirrors this batch's own Net Current Liquidity Surplus, so it tests little that is new.

This is a cosmetic re-parameterization of the archived "Self-Funding Cash Stock Value" and "Liquid Platform Productivity Value" (identical oibdp/(cogs+xsga) productivity leg, with the numerator's oancf/xsga merely swapped for oibdp−xint), so it adds no new economic content.

Structurally identical to the archived "Cash-Buffered Sales Productivity" with sale→revt−cogs and che/at→che/(at+dlc), which are trivial denominator/numerator tweaks rather than a substantive response to the diagnosed FMB-vs-alpha divergence.

It overlaps heavily with the archived "Short-Debt Coverage Liquidity Value" on the cash-to-enterprise-value leg, but charging both interest and expensed R&D against operating profit on assets is a genuinely different quality hurdle not yet tested in this archive, so it is worth one run.

The valuation leg is plain earnings-to-price (a long-published anomaly) and the quality leg is internally inconsistent — oibdp/(|pi|+xint) is mechanically maximized by firms with near-zero pretax income, i.e. it rewards exactly the non-core/transitory-earnings firms the hypothesis claims to exclude.

Near-duplicate of the archived "Intangible Platform Glamour Fade" (same market-cap-over-intangible-platform ratio times negated margin), with cash added to the denominator and the margin denominator changed — a cosmetic variant of an already-evaluated signal.

Coherent and directionally consistent, but it is the third pass at the archive's leverage×weak-profitability family (Debt-Overhang Profit Drain, Current-Debt Interest Trap) and largely re-expresses the well-known distress/leverage anomaly without diagnosing why those predecessors delivered negative alpha alongside positive FMB slopes.

The cash-to-price leg replicates the already-tested Net-Cash/Short-Debt liquidity legs and the "fixed-charge" denominator (xsga+xint) is really an SG&A-intensity rescaling already captured by Liquid Platform Productivity Value, making this a cosmetic denominator swap within a saturated family rather than a new mechanism.

The first leg is literally identical to Short-Debt Coverage Liquidity Value's liquidity leg and the second is a cash-conversion (inverse-accruals) ratio close to the already-failed Cash-Converted EBITDA Claim Value, with the ABS(oibdp) denominator further scrambling interpretation for loss-making firms.

It is essentially a double sort of two known anomalies (earnings yield and cash holdings), but it usefully inverts the archive's structure by putting profitability in the valuation leg and cash as the conditioner, which is a legitimate diagnostic of where the liquidity family's power originates.

The liquidity leg is byte-for-byte the Net Current Liquidity Surplus leg and the profitability leg is the RnD-Hurdle Liquidity Value numerator with only the scaling denominator changed from at to xsga+xrd, so this is a recombination of two archived signals rather than a new hypothesis.

This is a near-duplicate of Cash-Runway Glamour Burn (same NEG after-interest profitability leg plus xrd, valuation denominator che+dlc swapped for sale+che) and of Intangible Platform Glamour Fade, offering no mechanism beyond the already-documented expensive-and-unprofitable short.

Expensive-assets × weak-post-depreciation-profitability is the standard value×profitability interaction (already probed by Glamour Profit Fade), and adding che to at in the denominator double-counts cash that is already inside total assets, so the valuation leg's economic meaning is muddled.

This is the archive's best performer (Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield) with `xrd` subtracted from the numerator — a cosmetic merge with the already-tested R&D-hurdle family that changes nothing for the majority of firms where `xrd` is missing/zero, so it cannot cleanly attribute any incremental effect.

The primary leg is book-equity growth scaled by market value, whose positive expected sign contradicts the well-documented investment/asset-growth anomaly (and will be partly absorbed by CMA in the FF5 alpha), while the `ABS(DELTA(ceq)-ib)` penalty conflates issuance and repurchase — two effects with opposite known return signs.

The interaction is coherent and explicitly diagnoses the earlier After-Interest Claim Yield failure (strong slope, no alpha) as leverage-driven cheapness, though the conditioning leg is essentially the known debt-issuance anomaly, so any success may be attributable to that rather than to the interaction.

It retains the archive's strongest structure but adds a genuinely new, evidence-motivated dimension (capital-consumption burden) to explain why depreciation-based value legs produced negative alphas; the risk is that `dp/at` largely proxies industry capital intensity rather than value-trap risk.

The valuation leg collapses to a near-standard earnings yield (dividends are small relative to `ib` for most firms), and the conditioning SUMRANK of operating profitability plus cash cushion replicates the already-tested Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield family, so the marginal information content is minimal.

This is a rescaled recombination of two already-evaluated archive signals (Rising Interest Cost Profit Trap and Intangible Platform Glamour Fade), swapping the denominator to sales without introducing a new economic mechanism.

Internally consistent and mechanically clean, but it is just the archive's Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield with its numerator replaced by the already-tested Core-Consistency Operating Yield (fmb 2.4, alpha ≈ 0), so the most likely outcome is a mild dilution of a known result rather than new evidence.

It reuses the exact template of the archive's Low-Depreciation Cash Operating Yield — MUL(operating yield, SUMRANK(cash cushion, X)) — merely swapping X from -dp/at to -Δdebt/at, and the debt-change term was already shown to add little in Deleveraging Residual Claim Yield.

This is the archive's Profit-Funded Equity Payout Yield with the same ubiquitous cash-cushion term appended via SUMRANK, an incremental add-on rather than a substantively different mechanism, and the ib−Δceq construct is itself a well-known net-payout-yield proxy.

The gross-profit coverage of SG&A plus interest is a genuinely new conditioning term (distinct from prior SG&A-intensity and interest-trend variants) and the sign logic is coherent, though it is partly mechanically redundant with the operating margin already embedded in the operating-income yield leg.

Sign direction and expression are internally consistent, and the sale-plus-cash denominator combined with an explicit cash-drawdown term is a materially different construction from the prior glamour-fade signals, though it sits in a family where past fmb and alpha evidence has repeatedly disagreed.

The valuation leg is identical to the archive's best-performing "Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield," but the conditioner is genuinely re-specified from a balance-sheet stock ratio to a flow-based cash-runway coverage measure, which is a defensible economic distinction worth one test, though the expected incremental information is modest.

This is essentially "Operating-Income Cash Cushion Yield" with an identical second leg and interest merely subtracted from the numerator — a cosmetic tweak on a channel the archive has already probed repeatedly (After-Interest Claim Yield, Net Current Liquidity Surplus, Core Margin Floor), so it is unlikely to be informative about anything new.

Wrapping IND_ADJ around the dp/at term of the earlier "Low-Depreciation Cash Operating Yield" is precisely the cosmetic variant the objective warns against, and it is implausible that sector demeaning of one SUMRANK component explains a fmb_tstat of −1.041 coexisting with a +4.74 alpha t-stat — that disagreement points to composition/weighting or size-tilt issues, not industry effects.

Conditioning cheap post-depreciation operating income on industry-adjusted asset turnover introduces a genuinely new (DuPont-efficiency) conditioner not yet in the archive and is internally consistent, though value×turnover interactions are close to well-documented profitability-value territory and the conditioner is a low-frequency, slow-moving variable.

The parent "Cash-Burn Revenue Overprice" already produced a fmb_tstat of 0.02 with only a modest negative alpha, and swapping oibdp/sale for oiadp/at inside the same SUMRANK is a minor accounting substitution rather than a diagnosis of why the cross-sectional evidence collapsed.

Piling a fourth term onto an already-failed composite via nested SUMRANK (which silently assigns half weight to the profitability term and a quarter each to the others) is kitchen-sink construction, and the added rising-interest × weak-profitability leg duplicates the archive's "Rising Interest Cost Profit Trap."
